instructions: Tear the 4 injera into pieces about 1 inch across and put them in a big bowl. Day-old injera works best. Fresh injera turns soft faster.
Finely chop the onion and dice the 2 tomatoes. Mince the 3 garlic cloves. Peel and finely grate the ginger. That should be about 1 tbsp.
Heat the 3 tbsp oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until it's soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute, until they smell fragrant.
Stir in the 1 tbsp berbere and 2 tbsp tomato paste and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring all the time, until the paste darkens. If it starts to catch, add a splash of water.
Add the tomatoes and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and cook for 3 minutes, until they start to soften.
Pour in 1 cup water and bring it to a bubble. Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, until it looks like a thick tomato soup.
Meanwhile, slice the jalapeño into thin rings and put them in a small bowl for the table.
Turn the heat to low and add the injera. Fold it through the sauce for 1 to 2 minutes, until it's soaked up the sauce and is warm all the way through. Fold gently so the pieces keep their shape.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve hot, with the jalapeño on the side.
method_notes: Both versions soften onion with garlic in oil, make a loose tomato and berbere sauce, then fold torn injera through it off a low heat until it soaks up the sauce, with jalapeño in the mix or on top. BitterSweet cooks fresh tomato, ginger and jalapeño with the onion and loosens it with tomato sauce, while Messy Vegan Cook whisks berbere paste, tomato paste, wine and lemon with water and adds dates. Neither had 20 ratings (Messy Vegan Cook shows 5 from 1 vote) and the trusted cook for the cuisine has no Ethiopian recipes, so this follows BitterSweet with tomato paste and water in place of tomato sauce, and moves the jalapeño to the table.
